scenes.tts: A fruit fly and a frog look nothing alike. Do they build a nervous system the same way?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Fly Turned Over. A fly embryo and a frog embryo side by side. Question on screen.
scenes.narration: A fruit fly and a frog look nothing alike. Do they build a nervous system the same way?

scenes.tts: The fly has the same pair. Its gene decapentaplegic encodes a relative of B M P two and four.
scenes.caption: The fly has the same pair. Its gene decapentaplegic encodes a relative of BMP2 and 4.
scenes.visual: Fly embryo cross-section. Label: dpp, decapentaplegic, a BMP2/4 relative.
scenes.narration: The fly has the same pair. Its gene decapentaplegic encodes a relative of BMP2 and 4.

scenes.tts: And short gastrulation, or Sog, encodes a relative of Chordin.
scenes.visual: Label: sog, short gastrulation, a Chordin relative.
scenes.narration: And short gastrulation, or Sog, encodes a relative of Chordin.

scenes.tts: So D P P plays the part of the frog's B M P four. Sog plays the part of its Chordin.
scenes.caption: So Dpp plays the part of the frog's BMP4. Sog plays the part of its Chordin.
scenes.visual: Matching pairs drawn between the embryos: Dpp with BMP4, Sog with Chordin.
scenes.narration: So Dpp plays the part of the frog's BMP4. Sog plays the part of its Chordin.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-five, Holley and colleagues swapped the two antagonists between species.
scenes.caption: In 1995, Holley and colleagues swapped the two antagonists between species.
scenes.visual: Label: 1995, Holley and colleagues, fly and frog laboratories.
scenes.narration: In 1995, Holley and colleagues swapped the two antagonists between species.

scenes.tts: Frog Chordin works in the fly. And fly Sog works in the frog.
scenes.visual: Arrows cross between the two embryos: Chordin into the fly, Sog into the frog. Both work.
scenes.narration: Frog Chordin works in the fly. And fly Sog works in the frog.

scenes.tts: Tolloid was first named as a fly gene, and it cuts Sog.
scenes.visual: A Tolloid protease cuts Sog in the fly embryo.
scenes.narration: Tolloid was first named as a fly gene, and it cuts Sog.

scenes.tts: Now the map. In the fly, D P P is made on the dorsal side.
scenes.caption: Now the map. In the fly, Dpp is made on the dorsal side.
scenes.visual: Fly cross-section: Dpp colored on the dorsal side.
scenes.narration: Now the map. In the fly, Dpp is made on the dorsal side.

scenes.tts: Sog is made in broad lateral stripes of ectoderm on the ventral half.
scenes.visual: Sog colored in broad lateral stripes on the ventral half of the fly cross-section.
scenes.narration: Sog is made in broad lateral stripes of ectoderm on the ventral half.

scenes.tts: Use the rule. Where should the fly's nerve cord form?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: where does the nerve cord form?
scenes.narration: Use the rule. Where should the fly's nerve cord form?

scenes.tts: Ventrally, from that ectoderm, where Sog keeps D P P signaling low.
scenes.caption: Ventrally, from that ectoderm, where Sog keeps Dpp signaling low.
scenes.visual: The ventral ectoderm turns neural blue; a nerve cord forms there. Label: ventral nerve cord.
scenes.narration: Ventrally, from that ectoderm, where Sog keeps Dpp signaling low.

scenes.tts: The picture is simplified. The ventral-most fly cells are mesoderm, not nerve cord.
scenes.visual: The very bottom strip of the fly cross-section shades as mesoderm, beneath the neural stripes.
scenes.narration: The picture is simplified. The ventral-most fly cells are mesoderm, not nerve cord.

scenes.tts: In a vertebrate, B M P four signaling is high on the ventral side.
scenes.caption: In a vertebrate, BMP4 signaling is high on the ventral side.
scenes.visual: Frog cross-section beside the fly: BMP4 signaling high ventrally.
scenes.narration: In a vertebrate, BMP4 signaling is high on the ventral side.

scenes.tts: Chordin comes from the dorsal organizer, and the neural tube forms dorsally.
scenes.visual: Chordin colored dorsally; the neural tube forms on the dorsal side of the frog.
scenes.narration: Chordin comes from the dorsal organizer, and the neural tube forms dorsally.

scenes.tts: In both animals, nervous system forms where the antagonist keeps the B M P signal low.
scenes.caption: In both animals, nervous system forms where the antagonist keeps the BMP signal low.
scenes.visual: Both cross-sections: neural tissue sits under the antagonist in each.
scenes.narration: In both animals, nervous system forms where the antagonist keeps the BMP signal low.

scenes.tts: What happens if you turn the fly over?
scenes.visual: Question on screen: turn the fly over?
scenes.narration: What happens if you turn the fly over?

scenes.tts: Its B M P and its antagonist lie where a frog's do. The two maps line up.
scenes.caption: Its BMP and its antagonist lie where a frog's do. The two maps line up.
scenes.visual: The fly cross-section rotates; its Dpp, Sog and nerve cord colors align with the frog's.
scenes.narration: Its BMP and its antagonist lie where a frog's do. The two maps line up.

scenes.tts: In nineteen ninety-six, De Robertis and Sasai argued the common ancestor already patterned its body this way.
scenes.caption: In 1996, De Robertis and Sasai argued the common ancestor already patterned its body this way.
scenes.visual: Label: 1996, De Robertis and Sasai. A simple ancestral animal with BMP on one side and a Chordin-like antagonist on the other.
scenes.narration: In 1996, De Robertis and Sasai argued the common ancestor already patterned its body this way.

scenes.tts: One lineage then inverted the plan.
scenes.visual: The ancestor splits into two lineages; one flips over.
scenes.narration: One lineage then inverted the plan.

scenes.tts: On this view, the fly's map and the frog's map are one ancestral map, read from opposite sides.
scenes.visual: The two cross-sections merge into one ancestral cross-section, then separate again, one flipped.
scenes.narration: On this view, the fly's map and the frog's map are one ancestral map, read from opposite sides.

scenes.tts: Long before, in the eighteen twenties, Etienne Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire had proposed this inversion from anatomy alone.
scenes.caption: Long before, in the 1820s, Étienne Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire had proposed this inversion from anatomy alone.
scenes.visual: Label: 1820s, Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire. An old anatomical drawing of an arthropod beside a vertebrate.
scenes.narration: Long before, in the 1820s, Étienne Geoffroy Saint-Hilaire had proposed this inversion from anatomy alone.

scenes.tts: The takeaway: fly and frog run the same contest, B M P against its catcher, on opposite sides of the body.
scenes.caption: The takeaway: fly and frog run the same contest, BMP against its catcher. Only the body plan is upside down.
scenes.visual: Fly and frog cross-sections side by side, one flipped. Takeaway on screen.
scenes.narration: The takeaway: fly and frog run the same contest, BMP against its catcher. Only the body plan is upside down.
